key_points: hash table with chaining gives O(1) lookup by key
doubly linked list tracks recency so the LRU victim (tail) is found/removed in O(1)
each entry is simultaneously in a hash chain and in the recency list (intrusive links)
copies the value, allocates an entry, inserts into bucket and at list head
loop evicts from the tail until both count and byte limits are satisfied
eviction callback is invoked for each victim
pp points at the link that points to the current node (bucket slot or a previous node's hash_next)
unlinking is *pp = e->hash_next without special-casing the head of the chain
put copies the value in; get copies it out; caller never holds a pointer into the cache
cache frees its copies on delete, evict, expire, destroy
key is copied into a fixed-size inline array

bugs.title: Use-after-free in evict_tail
bugs.description: entry_free(victim) is called before the eviction callback, but the callback is passed victim->key, victim->value and victim->value_len, all of which are now freed memory.
bugs.fix: Invoke the callback first (or copy the needed fields), then free the entry.

bugs.title: Use-after-free of loop iterator in lru_purge_expired
bugs.description: drop_expired() frees e, then the for-loop increment reads e->prev from freed memory.
bugs.fix: Save prev = e->prev before the (possible) drop, then advance with prev.

bugs.title: Expiry path never decrements bytes_used; accounting drift can cause an infinite loop
bugs.description: evict_tail and lru_delete subtract value_len from bytes_used; drop_expired does not. Each expiry leaks accounting. Eventually bytes_used > max_bytes even when the cache is empty, and the while loop in lru_put calls evict_tail forever (it returns immediately when tail == NULL), spinning while holding the mutex.
bugs.fix: Subtract e->value_len in drop_expired (ideally factor one shared 'remove_entry' helper used by delete/evict/expire). Also make the eviction loop terminate when the list is empty.

bugs.title: Key length off-by-one and unterminated key via strncpy
bugs.description: key[] holds LRU_MAX_KEY_LEN bytes including the NUL, so the longest valid key is 63 chars. The check rejects only strlen > 64, so a 64-char key passes; strncpy then copies 64 bytes with no terminator. Later strcmp/hash_key over e->key read past the array into adjacent fields (value pointer bytes).
bugs.fix: Reject strlen(key) >= LRU_MAX_KEY_LEN, and/or copy with explicit termination (memcpy + e->key[len] = '\0').

bugs.title: Updating an existing key does not refresh its recency
bugs.description: The in-place update branch never calls list_move_front. A just-written entry can sit at the tail and be the first eviction victim, violating LRU semantics (including evicting the entry that was just written).
bugs.fix: Call list_move_front(c, e) in the update branch.

bugs.title: Leak of cache struct when bucket allocation fails
bugs.description: On calloc failure for buckets the function returns NULL without freeing c.

bugs.title: Bucket array leaked in lru_destroy
bugs.description: Entries and the cache struct are freed but c->buckets is never freed.

bugs.title: lru_hit_ratio: integer division, divide-by-zero, and unsynchronized read
bugs.description: hits and misses are uint64_t so the division is integer division: result is 0 unless hits == total. If both are zero, it is an integer divide-by-zero (SIGFPE). Stats are also read without taking the lock while workers update them (data race).
bugs.fix: Lock, snapshot hits/misses, return 0.0 if total == 0, otherwise (double)hits / (double)total.

bugs.title: lru_get dereferences out_len without validating it
bugs.description: The argument check validates c, key, out but not out_len, which is written unconditionally (NULL dereference). The ENOSPC path also reports 'required size' but does not count as a hit or touch recency.
bugs.fix: Validate out_len or make it optional.

bugs.title: Zero-length values fail spuriously
bugs.description: malloc(0) may legally return NULL, which is then reported as -ENOMEM; also `!value` rejects NULL for len == 0. Empty values are valid in many use cases.

anchors: every get mutates the recency list so a read-write lock does not help
shard the cache by hash into N independent caches/locks
approximate LRU (CLOCK / sampled) to avoid list update on every hit
re-entrancy deadlock if callback calls lru_* (non-recursive mutex)
collect victims and invoke callbacks after unlocking
copy-out is safe against concurrent eviction/free
cost grows with value size and adds memcpy under the lock
refcounted values or handles allow zero-copy reads
caller must size buffer; ENOSPC protocol requires retry
bytes_used counts only value payload, not key, entry struct, malloc overhead, buckets
count entry overhead for a real budget
lazy expiry leaves dead entries consuming space until touched or purged
purge is O(n) under the lock
expired entries can crowd out live ones before they reach the LRU tail
alternatives: timer wheel / heap, periodic background sweeper, check tail on put

expected_themes.theme: factor one remove_entry() helper used by delete/evict/expire to keep accounting in one place
add tests: sanitizers (ASan/UBSan/TSan), Valgrind, stress test with invariant checks (count == list length == sum of chain lengths, bytes_used == sum of value_len)
API clarity: size_t-aware lru_get that returns a length or allocates, optional out_len, documented thread-safety and lifecycle
sharding or finer-grained locking; background expiry; monotonic clock
make key length dynamic or documented; enforce limits at one place

red_herrings.description: list_unlink / list_push_front / list_move_front (correct, handle head/tail/one-element cases)
nbuckets = capacity with LRU_MIN_BUCKETS floor (intentional, load factor <= 1)
lru_put's error paths free `copy` correctly (no leak on the -ENOMEM path for the entry allocation)
evict loop evicting multiple entries in one put (intentional; a big value can displace several small ones)
hash_key unsigned overflow (well-defined for unsigned int)
worker() reusing buf for both lookup output and payload construction (sequential, no overlap)

items: lru_count reads count without the lock (data race) and does not NULL-check c (lines 409-412)
hash_key uses plain `char`: sign extension of bytes >= 0x80 makes hashing platform-dependent (line 83)
TTL uses wall-clock time(); clock adjustments (NTP, manual) can expire entries early or keep them alive; CLOCK_MONOTONIC is preferable (lines 272, 337, 396)
is_expired uses `<`, so an entry is still valid during the second equal to its expiry; boundary semantics are undocumented (line 95)
now + ttl_secs can overflow on 32-bit time_t with large ttl (lines 288, 300)
lru_destroy gives no protection against other threads still blocked on or about to take the mutex (lifecycle contract is undocumented)

grader_instructions: Grade against the rubric; do not require exact wording. Accept any answer whose meaning matches an anchor.
Credit bugs by function name or approximate line (+/- 5 lines).
Distinguish 'identified symptom' from 'identified root cause'; full bug credit requires the root cause.
For design questions, reward reasoned trade-offs over buzzwords; an answer that names sharding without explaining why a single lock is limiting earns at most half.
Report: per-section score, list of bugs found / missed, false positives, and one actionable suggestion for improving the candidate's code-reading approach.
